clue.text: Attempt to incorporate a trial in a wall-hanging

indicators.note: to incorporate is to take into the body of something, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: to attempt is to have a try
a trial, in the sense of a nuisance, is a pest

explanation.surface: Someone tries to work a sample or trial piece into a decorative wall-hanging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trial' looks like an experiment, but here it means a trying person: a pest.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapestry is a woven textile picture traditionally hung on walls of grand houses.

clue.text: Go and hide a defector

blocks.note: a go is a turn, as in 'your go'
an animal's hide is its coat

explanation.surface: Someone told to run and hide from a deserter.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'Go' and 'hide' look like verbs but are nouns here.
explanation.definitionFit: A turncoat is someone who deserts one side for the opposing party, a traitor.

clue.text: A point in support of this sort of spinning?

definitions.text: A point in support of this sort of spinning?

blocks.clueFragment: A point in support of this sort of spinning?
blocks.note: surface reading: an argument backing some kind of yarn-making or spin-doctoring
setter's reading: a ballet dancer balanced on the tip of one toe while turning round

explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' looks like a debating point, but ballet dancers turn on point, the tips of their toes.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a full turn of the body made by a dancer balanced on one foot, often on the toes.

clue.text: Rift makes us give away secrets

blocks.note: first meaning: a crack or division
second meaning: to inform on accomplices

explanation.surface: A quarrel drives us to reveal confidences.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a breach between parties and, informally, to betray companions by informing.

clue.text: A small state's only source of nourishment

blocks.note: RI is Rhode Island, the smallest US state, plus 's
sole means only, as in 'the sole survivor'

explanation.surface: A tiny country relies on a single supply of food.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhode Island is the smallest state of the USA, abbreviated RI.
explanation.definitionFit: A rissole is a fried cake of minced meat or fish, so a modest example of food.

clue.text: Sort of cake for a heavy drinker

blocks.note: first meaning: a light airy cake made with eggs
second meaning: someone who soaks up alcohol

explanation.surface: Choosing a suitable cake to serve a guest who drinks a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria sponge is a classic cake type, and a soak who absorbs liquor is informally called this.

clue.text: Reportedly outspoken actor branching out in London?

indicators.note: reportedly means going by what is heard, so a word spoken the same is wanted

blocks.note: plain-spoken means frank
Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a famous Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: A blunt-talking actor is said to be expanding into new work in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Branching out' sounds like a career move, but it describes the literal branches.
explanation.definitionFit: The London plane is the hardy hybrid tree lining the capital's streets and squares, so it branches there.

clue.text: Race in north, always well turned out

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits within it, so the race goes inside

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for north
ay (or aye) is an old word for always
the TT, Tourist Trophy, is the Isle of Man motorcycle race

explanation.surface: Someone who always dresses smartly for a race up north.
explanation.walkthrough: N + A(TT)Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty means neat and smartly dressed, a fair synonym for someone well turned out.

clue.text: Former quote to bring into play

blocks.note: ex means former, as in ex-husband
to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: An earlier citation is used to bring a point into an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: To excite is to stir into activity or set in motion, as with exciting an electrical circuit.

clue.text: Revolutionary body administered university in America

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the country's abbreviation

blocks.note: to run something is to administer it
U is the abbreviation for university
the United States

explanation.surface: A rebel group ran an American college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests rebels, but a planet revolves around the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Uranus is the seventh planet, a heavenly body that revolves in orbit around the sun.

clue.text: Like a dean, possibly, describing Cobbett's rides

blocks.note: first meaning: a ... dean is a Church of England clergyman overseeing a group of country parishes
second meaning: William Cobbett's book of journeys through English countryside is titled ... Rides

explanation.surface: Comparing a clergyman with the horseback journeys of a famous English writer.
explanation.walkthrough: William Cobbett was an early-nineteenth-century English radical journalist whose horseback tours of farming country became a celebrated book.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means belonging to the countryside, fitting both the church title and Cobbett's book title.

clue.text: Bitter snow at first when in the far north

indicators.note: what comes at first is the opening letter of the word snow
one piece sits in another, so the word when goes inside the far north

blocks.note: the opening letter of snow
the polar region at the top of the globe
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Biting cold snow falls first in the polar regions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bitter' looks like a description of the polar weather, but it is the definition, meaning cutting in tone.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarcastic remarks are cutting and resentful, so bitter is a fair synonym for the mocking tone.

clue.text: Final moments before youth leader leaves part of Northern Ireland?

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of youth is wanted
whatever leaves departs, so that letter is taken out of the place name

blocks.note: the opening letter of youth
County Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: The last minutes before a young leader departs from part of Ulster.
explanation.definitionFit: A countdown is the closing sequence of seconds counted off before a launch or deadline.

clue.text: College servant held by eight extremists in the republic

indicators.note: extremists sit at the extremes, so only the two end letters of eight are kept
something held by another is gripped inside it

blocks.note: the first and last letters of eight
a gyp is a college servant at Cambridge

explanation.surface: A college porter is held captive by eight extremists somewhere in a republic.
explanation.walkthrough: Gyp is the Cambridge word for a college servant; Durham has the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is an example of a republic, the Arab Republic of Egypt since 1953.

clue.text: A northern tree, sound and old

indicators.note: sound tells us to go by how the word for the tree is pronounced, not spelt

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for northern
teak is a hardwood tree; the French-style ending is said the same way

explanation.surface: A northern tree is described as healthy and very old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like 'healthy' describing the tree, but it signals a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: Antique as an adjective means belonging to former times, a synonym for old.

clue.text: Still tight-lipped about embarrassing incident out east

indicators.note: out means removed, so the compass point is dropped
about means surrounding, so the first word is placed around the second

blocks.note: keeping quiet, saying nothing
making a scene is an embarrassing public display
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Someone stays silent about an awkward episode in the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like 'nevertheless' opening the sentence, but it is the adjective meaning motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: Quiescent means at rest and inactive, the adjectival sense of motionless or calm.

clue.text: Writer's resting-place in Kent, perhaps

indicators.note: something in a place is enclosed within it, so one word sits inside the other

blocks.note: Kent is a county in south-east England, abbreviated SE
a crib is a bed, a place to rest

explanation.surface: An author's grave or home lies somewhere in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks Kent as one example of the south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe is a copyist or author, someone who writes for a living.

clue.text: But we would touch the bank with it!

definitions.text: But we would touch the bank with it!

blocks.clueFragment: But we would touch the bank with it!
blocks.note: surface reading: a defiant twist on the saying that you would not touch something with this
setter's reading: a bargee pushes off against the riverbank with a long pole

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'I wouldn't touch it with a ...' is turned round: on a canal, bargees really do touch the bank with one.
explanation.definitionFit: This long pole is used by boatmen to push a barge along or fend it off from the canal bank.

clue.text: Sad news accepted in factory

indicators.note: something accepted in is taken within, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: a plant is an industrial works
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Unhappy tidings are received at a works.
explanation.walkthrough: PLAN(GEN)T.
explanation.definitionFit: Plangent describes a mournful, resonant sound, so it suits a melancholy or sorrowful tone.

clue.text: Celebrity entertaining, for instance, a lot of soldiers

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to hold them in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a literary lion is a celebrated person
e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'

explanation.surface: A famous person puts on a show for a large group of troops.
explanation.walkthrough: A literary lion is a celebrity, a sense dating from the lions of the Tower of London shown to visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: A legion was a Roman army unit of several thousand men, so a large body of troops.

clue.text: Delicious drink somehow producing trance

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wonderful drink that somehow puts you into a daze.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar was the drink of the Greek gods, and the word now means any delicious beverage.

clue.text: More than one, say, of the coats in the chest

definitions.text: of the coats in the chest

indicators.note: say asks for a word spoken like the one before it, not spelt like it

blocks.note: the grammatical term for more than one

explanation.surface: Several layers of clothing are found folded in a chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coats' and 'chest' suggest clothes stored in a trunk, but they are the membranes in the ribcage.
explanation.definitionFit: The pleurae are the two membranes lining the lungs and thoracic cavity, and the adjective describes them.

clue.text: Airborne soldier died without a vote — what an anomaly!

blocks.note: a para is a paratrooper
d. is the abbreviation for died
without anything is with nothing, the zero O
a vote is marked with a cross on the ballot paper

explanation.surface: A paratrooper died without ever voting, which seems strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like a container signal, but it simply gives nothing, the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A paradox is a seemingly self-contradictory situation, so an anomaly, something that defies expectation.

clue.text: Old ways to limit this sadness

indicators.note: to limit is to bound on all sides, so the second word encloses the first

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
paths are ways or routes

explanation.surface: Traditional habits set bounds on someone's grief.
explanation.walkthrough: PATH(O)S.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathos is the quality in art or life that evokes pity and sorrow in the audience.

clue.text: Paper rejecting leading article about German leader is the Scotsman

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of German is wanted
leading means coming first, so only the opening letter of article is wanted
about means surrounding, so the paper goes around the German's first letter
rejecting means throwing back, so the assembled letters are read the other way

blocks.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
the opening letter of German
the opening letter of article

explanation.surface: A newspaper rejects an editorial about a German politician; The Scotsman is the paper in question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Scotsman' looks like the Edinburgh newspaper, but it means a typical Scottish man. SU(G)N + A, reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Angus is a traditional Scottish first name, used here to stand for a typical man from Scotland.

clue.text: Porridge for a semi-Rabelaisian figure

indicators.note: semi means half, so only half of the giant's name is kept

blocks.note: Pantagruel is the giant hero of Rabelais's comic novels

explanation.surface: Oatmeal served to a coarsely comic character.
explanation.walkthrough: The ten-letter name is cut in half and the second five letters are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruel is a thin porridge of oats or meal boiled in water or milk.

clue.text: Sea trip? A bribe is able to secure it

indicators.note: to trip is to stumble, so the letters fall into a new arrangement
to secure something is to hold it fast inside, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: can means is able to
the six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wants a sea cruise and hopes a bribe will get them a place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea trip' reads as a cruise, but the definition is just 'Sea'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribbean is the tropical body of water bordered by the West Indies and Central America.

clue.text: Extra payment for journalist sent up to cover cricket side

indicators.note: in a down answer, sent up means written from bottom to top
to cover is to go over and around, so the turned word encloses the next

blocks.note: a sub is a sub-editor
the on side is the leg side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A reporter earns extra pay for being sent to report on a cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the on (leg) side.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonus is an extra sum paid on top of normal wages as a reward.

clue.text: Domestic servant forced, say, to join the audience

indicators.note: say asks for a word spoken like forced, not spelt like it
joining means placing side by side, so one word is attached to the other

blocks.note: a theatre audience is the house, as in 'a full house'
made means forced, as in 'made to do it'

explanation.surface: A servant is compelled to sit with the spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone piece comes second in the answer though first in the clue: it joins the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A housemaid is a female domestic employee who cleans and tidies a household's rooms.

clue.text: Pooter, otherwise identified, in a casino on Euston Road

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the following words, running across their boundaries

blocks.note: the end of casino, all of on and the start of Euston
surface padding completing the London street name

explanation.surface: A comic Victorian clerk turns up, under another name, in a London gaming house.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Pooter is the hero of The Diary of a Nobody by George and Weedon Grossmith, so 'otherwise identified' he is a nobody.
explanation.definitionFit: Pooter is famously a nobody, and a nobody is someone of no importance, a mere cipher.

clue.text: Greet head of State with a musical instrument

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of State
taken as written
a lute is a pear-shaped stringed instrument

explanation.surface: Welcoming a head of state with a musical fanfare.
explanation.definitionFit: To salute someone is to acknowledge or welcome them with a formal gesture.

clue.text: Scope for protecting one's living

indicators.note: protecting means shielding all round, so the first word wraps the second

blocks.note: scope is range or extent
one is I, and 's is is

explanation.surface: Room to safeguard one's livelihood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Living' looks like a livelihood, but it is the adjective meaning alive.
explanation.definitionFit: Existent means having real being, currently alive or present in the world.
